what: General, genre-agnostic craft recipes for the visual skills Apple MAX was measured weak at (gauntlet rounds 1-4: flat UI without outlines/gradients/cartoon fonts, collapsed cards, missing-glyph icons, maps that are a ground plus one template, flat lighting). Every value is expressed through tools Apple already has and properties the plugin allowlist accepts. Grounded in the Roblox Creator Docs pages listed per card (local corpus packages/corpus/data/chunks.jsonl, mirrored from github.com/Roblox/creator-docs). Nothing here names or describes a specific game.

cards.title: Game UI from the stored library: pick components, fill them in, place them, check them
recipe: Every visible UI piece is one insert_ui_component call (D-UIONLY-1). The library draws it from stored 9-slice panels, buttons, bars and icons with its own outline, depth and display font, so it reads as a finished game, not grey boxes.
Pick the skin once with genre (simulator/tycoon/pet, obby/parkour, adventure/horror/rpg, shooter/fighting) and use the same genre and colour on every piece.

Component per job: currency_counter or stat_counter for top balance pills (icon coin, gem...), button_icon for round side buttons down the left edge, button_primary for the main action, shop_window, inventory_grid or item_card for card grids (items fill the cards, so none collapses), daily_reward, dialog_confirm, notification_toast for popups, settings_window, button_close on every window.
Place with anchor (top_left, left, center...) and position/size as screen fractions: counters at the top clear of the Roblox top bar, side rail at the left, windows at center.
Pictures are icon keys (coin, gem, star, heart, gear, trophy, cart, lock, gift...). Never type emoji or symbols into Text: the font has no glyph and they render as square tofu boxes.
Afterwards change only Text, Position, Size and Visible with set_properties; wire behaviour in a LocalScript that finds the piece by path (PlayerGui:WaitForChild(name)).
avoid: Creating ScreenGui, Frame, TextLabel, TextButton, ImageLabel, ImageButton, UIStroke, UICorner or UIGradient with create_instances or Instance.new: refused.
Setting colours, Font or Image on an inserted piece: refused.
Mixing skins, two pieces on one anchor, emoji in Text.
cards.check: check_ui_layout on phone and desktop reports nothing overlapping, off screen or zero-sized; inspect_visually shows library panels with readable text and drawn icons, no tofu squares.

cards.title: Compose a map in layers: landform, frame, paths, landmarks, props, dressing
recipe: 1 Landform: terrain, not a flat baseplate. shape_terrain heightmap (amplitude 0.15-0.3, scale 64-128) over the play area, then hide/remove the Baseplate. Keep the central play space gently rolling so players can walk it.

2 Frame: raise the edges — edit_terrain fill_ball/fill_block hills and rock cliffs (Enum.Material.Rock/Ground) around the perimeter, 30-80 studs tall, so the map has a skyline and a boundary instead of an endless plane.

3 Paths: 8-12 stud wide paths from spawn to each landmark (edit_terrain replace_material strips or flat Parts) curving to a central plaza. A channel or line of terrain along points is ONE edit_terrain call, action path (points, width, depth, fill Air, Water or a material).
4 Landmarks: a centrepiece at the plaza (statue, fountain, big sign) and one distinct building/structure per zone, each visible from spawn.

5 Props: from the model library or grouped into Models (see props card), place in clusters of 3-7 along paths and around landmarks, never evenly spread; fences follow path edges; lamps every 20-30 studs along paths.

6 Dressing: insert ONE of each tree, rock or bush (library, else built once from Parts), then clone_instances within an area (count, minSpacing 8-15, scale [0.8,1.3], yaw [0,360], seed) or along a path edge; scatter_instances suits rolling terrain. Then set_mood (overrides for the exact hour asked), render_view.
Budget by layer: a small hub is 150-250 studs across with 20-60 prop models, not one ground plane plus one template.
avoid: A single flat grass plate with one model on it.
Props floating or sunk (use scatter_instances ray drop, or read_terrain heights).
Uniform grid placement; everything the same size.
cards.check: render_view from spawn: foreground, midground and background all have content; audit_build/check_composition shows several prop groups and terrain relief.

cards.title: Low-poly props by the asset order: library first, then Parts in full detail (trees, rocks, fences, lamps)
recipe: The asset order of the system prompt applies: find_library_model (a plain noun: pine tree, rock, fence), insert_library_model (position = bottom centre, height in studs), then the Creator Store, then adapt or combine. With no hit or a failed insert, Parts is step 4, not a failure: build it in full detail as below.
Materials: SmoothPlastic (or Plastic) with saturated flat colours reads as stylised low-poly; 2-3 tones per prop (base, shade, accent). Anchored true, CastShadow true.

Round tree: trunk Part Shape Cylinder (rotate so its axis is vertical: Orientation [0,0,90]) 2x10x2, brown; canopy 2-3 overlapping Shape Ball parts 8-12 studs in two greens, offset so the silhouette is lumpy.
Pine tree: trunk cylinder + 3 stacked WedgePart/Part tiers shrinking upward (12 -> 8 -> 4 wide), each rotated 45 degrees from the one below, dark green.
Rock: 2-3 Parts with random Orientation, slightly different greys, partly sunk into the ground.
Fence: posts every 6-8 studs (1x4x1) + two rails (0.5x0.5xlength) between them, light wood colour; follow path edges.
Lamp: thin dark post, a small box/ball head with Material Neon warm yellow and a PointLight (Range 12-16, Brightness 1-2).

Build a prop ONCE: write its parts around (0,0,0) in one create_instances call with origin {at, yaw} and group {className: Model, name, primaryPart}, then repeat it with clone_instances at / along / within (positions, a line, an area; a seed repeats a layout). Never compute copy coordinates by hand.
avoid: One giant Part as a 'tree'.
Every prop identical in size and rotation.
Neon on large surfaces.
cards.check: render_view close-up: each prop reads as the object from 30 studs away; the Model count matches what was placed.

cards.title: Readable small buildings and stalls by the asset order: library first, then Parts in full detail
recipe: The asset order of the system prompt applies: find_library_model (house, shop, stall, hut), insert_library_model, then the Creator Store, then adapt or combine. With no fit or a failed insert, Parts is step 4: build it in full detail as below, once around (0,0,0) with create_instances origin and group, then repeat it with clone_instances at / along / within.
Footprint 14-24 studs; floor slab 1 stud tall, slightly larger than the walls.
Walls: 3 wall Parts + a front with an opening (two side pieces + a lintel) so players can see in; wall colour warm/light, trim darker.
Roof: two WedgePart halves meeting at a ridge (or one wedge for a lean-to), overhanging the walls by 1-2 studs, contrasting colour.
Awning/stall: a striped canopy from alternating coloured thin Parts (e.g. 4-6 stripes of two colours) tilted 10-20 degrees over the counter; counter Part at waist height (3 studs).
Sign: a Part above the door, then insert_ui_component with component surface_sign, parent that Part and text naming the building's function in one or two words.
Details that sell it: a door frame, 1-2 windows (lighter or Glass inset), barrels/crates beside the entrance, a lamp.
avoid: A single box with a label.
Roof flush with the walls (no overhang reads as a crate).
cards.check: render_view from the nearest path: the building's purpose is readable from its sign and silhouette.

cards.title: Light the scene with a mood instead of default flat lighting
recipe: Always finish a visual build with set_mood (sunny or day for bright stylised worlds, golden for warm, misty for depth, night/horror for dark) — then render_view to see it.
Bright stylised baseline if tuning by hand: Lighting ClockTime 13-14.5, Brightness 2-3, OutdoorAmbient raised (~[0.55,0.55,0.6]) so shadows are not black, ShadowSoftness 0.2-0.4.
Atmosphere: Density 0.25-0.35, Haze 0-1 for clear air (distance still fades), Color slightly blue; higher Density/Haze only for misty or eerie moods.

ColorCorrectionEffect: Saturation 0.1-0.25, Contrast 0.05-0.15 for cartoon vibrancy; BloomEffect Intensity 0.3-0.6, Threshold 1.5-2.5 so only bright things glow; optional SunRaysEffect Intensity 0.05-0.1.
Practical lights where the eye should go: warm PointLights on lamps/landmarks, Neon accents on interactables.
avoid: Leaving Lighting at defaults (flat, grey)
Fog so dense the landmarks disappear
Bloom threshold below 1 (everything glows)
cards.check: render_view before and after: after has visible shadows, coloured sky/haze and clear foreground/background separation.

cards.title: Turn a one-line idea into a complete game, in gated phases
recipe: 0 Brief first (propose_plan): pitch with a verb the player does, genre + proven references, core loop in 3 parts (minute-to-minute action, repeated action set, progression engine), the hook a clip could show in 10 s, social mechanic, mobile first, maturity target Minimal/Mild, 2-3 purchase ideas. Default scope tier S: one map, one loop, a few upgrades; everything else goes on an update list.

1 Scaffold: ReplicatedStorage Shared (one Config module holding every number) and Remotes; ServerScriptService services (Data, Economy, Progression, Round/Zone, Store); StarterPlayerScripts controllers. The server owns currency, damage and rewards; every remote is validated.
2 Greybox the loop with plain Parts: it must complete alone and with several clients, first reward in under 30 s. If it is not fun, change the loop before adding anything.

3 Vertical slice: one zone at final art (lighting, palette, materials), first upgrade, HUD, one sound set, one effect set, saving; the first 60 s is a guided path: spawn, a visual cue, first reward, a visible next goal.

4 MVP: short/mid/long goals visible, each currency has sources and sinks, daily reward with streak, a social hook (leaderboard, co-op bonus), a small store in Config, settings menu. A new player can play 20-30 min without a dead end.
5 Polish: every action gets a sound and a visual response; no grey placeholder or Part names near spawn.
6 QA: play_check, rejoin and leave mid-action, many clients, mobile layout; Output clean.
avoid: Placing parts before the brief names the loop, hook and scope.
Monetisation or rebirths in the first prototype.
Copying a hit's title or art: copy mechanics, change theme and hook.
cards.check: Each phase gate passed before the next: brief has all 3 loop parts; loop is fun in greybox; slice looks final; MVP gives 20-30 min of goals; Output is clean in play_check.

cards.title: Design the first 60 seconds and reasons to return for 28 days
recipe: Spawn the player next to an interactive object; first reward within 15-30 s; core loop shown by 60 s; the whole first-time experience under 5 min. Teach by context: at most two popups, then hints that appear just after the typical time a step takes.

Roblox ranks day 1, days 2-7 and days 8-28 separately: day 1 = a fun first session; days 2-7 = daily reward with a 7-day escalating streak, timers, a quest chain, a friend goal; days 8-28 = new zones or tiers unlocking around days 3, 7, 14, 21, collections, events.
Always show the next goal on screen (short, mid, long term). Early thresholds are low; reward moments get a sound, an effect and a number pop.
Build co-play in: shared goals, a group boost, an invite button wired to SocialService:PromptGameInvite.
Log the funnel on the server: AnalyticsService:LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent per step, LogEconomyEvent, LogProgressionStartEvent/CompleteEvent.
avoid: A text wall or long cutscene before play.
Gating play on opting in to notifications.
Designing for one marathon session: playtime counts up to 60 min per day.
cards.check: A stranger knows what to do in under 30 s without reading; a reward lands before 30 s; the next goal is always visible; funnel steps are logged.

cards.title: Add fair monetisation: passes, developer products, receipts, policy
recipe: A 100 Robux sale yields 70 Robux. Offer one cheap impulse item (about 25-75), considered items (100-250) and one flagship (400-1,000+); these tiers are third-party guidance. Keep promoted passes within 50-800 Robux.

Passes = permanent perks (check UserOwnsGamePassAsync on join and on PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished). Developer products = consumables, granted only in MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt: grant once per PurchaseId (record it in the save), return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is saved, else NotProcessedYet.
Read prices at runtime with GetProductInfo; never hard-code Robux in labels (managed and regional pricing change them).
Paid random items: show a percentage table summing to 100 before purchase and gate with PolicyService ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted; trading of paid items with IsPaidItemTradingAllowed.
Rewarded video: give a normal reward at a natural break, never Robux or random items, never gate core progression. Offer a private server price.
Place purchases in context (at the moment the item matters), not as popup loops.
avoid: Granting a product outside ProcessReceipt or more than once.
Pay-to-win that breaks the loop for free players.
Playable gambling, real-money stakes, off-platform links.
cards.check: Every product grants exactly once and survives rejoin; prices come from GetProductInfo; random items show odds and respect PolicyService.

cards.title: Prepare a publish-ready page: title, description, icon, thumbnails, rating
recipe: Title and description describe the real gameplay with the genre words players search; description = one-sentence premise, 3 key features, controls, what is coming.

Thumbnails: 3-5 distinct 16:9 shots at 1920x1080 of real gameplay (action shot, reward close-up, several avatars together, update banner); at least 2 active so Roblox personalises them. Icon 512x512 (author at 1024), one high-contrast subject, no small text, readable at 150x150. Frame these shots with render_view.
Answer the Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire from the real content and retake it after changes; Minimal or Mild reaches the widest audience.

Owner actions an AI cannot do: ID and age check, 2-step verification, Plus or the refundable fee for under-16 reach; new games start for 16+ and Trusted Friends. Tell the owner, and read the live publishing pages because thresholds change.
Start Private, then Limited for a beta, Public after the beta gate; plan an update every 1-2 weeks.
avoid: Free-Robux or giveaway wording, copied names or art, art the game does not deliver: all reduce reach.
cards.check: Every thumbnail and the icon show the real game; description has premise, features, controls; questionnaire matches content; owner actions listed.

cards.title: Vet every inserted model for malicious scripts before keeping it
recipe: Assets without scripts (meshes, images, audio) cannot carry code; models, packages and plugins can.

Block and review any Script, LocalScript or ModuleScript that has: require with a number, getfenv/setfenv, loadstring, InsertService:LoadAsset, text decoded with string.reverse, long \ddd escape strings, XOR or decompress loops, or a script hidden inside a Weld, Part or Sky.
Verified creators, ratings and sales are not proof of safety. Hundreds of nested oddly named children is a crash trap.
Keep LoadStringEnabled off and HTTP off unless a feature needs it; never grant SandboxedInstanceMode overrides to third-party assets.
Prefer writing the behaviour yourself over keeping a free script; keep only the meshes and parts.
avoid: Keeping an unread script from a free model.
Enabling LoadStringEnabled or HTTP for a model.
cards.check: No inserted script contains the patterns above; any script kept was read line by line.
